call_points.text: Revenue growth guided at 2x market growth, not an absolute number, citing volatility
FY27 capex plan of ₹300 Cr OSAT, ₹300 Cr PCB and ₹250 Cr EMS
OSAT received ₹170 Cr government subsidy till July 2026
Order book of more than ₹8,900 Cr; Q1 additions exceeded deliveries
Metering strategy to de-risk receivables to be detailed by the February call
Management called FY27 a difficult year on component availability and cost
OSAT Unit 1 is fully operational; Unit 2 is in commercialisation by Q2FY26.
Order book stated at over ₹9,000 Cr, described as healthy, diversified and non-cancellable.
OSAT revenue visibility of over ₹2,500 Cr over the next five years.
Q4 PAT fell partly on ₹32 Cr of intangible amortisation booked once a year; it will now be quarterly.
One large EV two-wheeler OEM cut volumes about 90%, which management cites as a main reason for the revenue miss.
Analysts pressed on the guidance miss and cash flow; management apologised and said it would be more careful with future commitments.
Mysore facility crossed ₹1,000 Cr in FY26 revenue.

guidance.statement: Will grow at double the market growth rate of 15-16%
PCB revenue of ₹300-400 Cr in FY27
OSAT revenue of ₹250-300 Cr in FY27
NPD-led and value-added solutions to reach nearly 30% of total revenue
Metering working capital to be reversed within 3 quarters; 70-80% of the ₹600 Cr negative cash flow reduced by Q3
Rail business to grow 20-25% this year with margins above 30%
OSAT and PCB combined revenue of ₹450-500 Cr
FY27 capex of ₹300 Cr OSAT, ₹300 Cr PCB and ₹250 Cr EMS

operating_notes.text: Metering subsidiary revenue was ₹971 Cr of FY26's ₹3,626 Cr, with receivables of ₹1,365 Cr, of which about ₹250 Cr is non-current.
Stand-alone EMS revenue was ₹2,655 Cr in FY26 with receivables of ₹399 Cr, up only ₹20 Cr from ₹379 Cr at the start of the year.
The pending metering order is about 35 lakh meters, roughly a ₹1,400 Cr order, with a possible 3.5-4 lakh meter extension.
Component prices rose 30-35% and PCB prices tripled, with lead times of 6-8 months.
Metering collections were ₹88 Cr against ₹240 Cr of sales in Q1FY27.
Receivable from the leading EV two-wheeler customer fell below ₹100 Cr.

watchlist.response: Management apologised, cited a 90% volume drop at a large EV OEM and delayed government orders, and said it would stop giving absolute numbers, committing only to doubling market growth.
watchlist.text: FY26 revenue of ₹3,626 Cr missed the ₹4,500 Cr and then ₹4,000 Cr guidance; analysts questioned the sanctity of guidance.

watchlist.response: Management said stand-alone EMS was ₹250 Cr positive and blamed metering installation delays; it targets 70-80% of the negative cash flow reversed by Q3 and positive by year-end.
watchlist.text: Operating cash flow was about ₹600 Cr negative against guidance of roughly neutral.

watchlist.response: Only about ₹40 Cr was discounted this quarter; management said banks need completed installation and billing, and it will stop taking AMISP-style orders.
watchlist.text: Metering receivables rose to ₹1,365 Cr despite a promised ₹250 Cr securitisation last quarter.

watchlist.response: Management said the market is volatile and it does not want to commit numbers it may miss; it was evasive on a specific figure.
Management said it is seriously evaluating options to de-risk receivables and will detail strategy by the February call, without committing to a divestment.
watchlist.text: Smart metering returns sub-optimal after two years; analysts asked about divesting the business

watchlist.response: Management gave an approximate ₹800 Cr and said exact numbers would follow.
